Look up on a sunny day, and the sky is blue.
But sunlight isn't blue at all.
It's every colour mixed together, travelling in waves.
Red light has long, lazy waves. Blue light has short, choppy ones.
When sunlight hits the air, tiny gas molecules bounce the short blue waves around far more than the red ones.
So blue light gets scattered across the whole sky, and reaches your eyes from every direction.
That's why, wherever you look, the sky is blue.
At sunset, the light travels through so much air that most of the blue is bounced away before it reaches you.
Only the reds and yellows make it through.
So the sky isn't painted blue. It's sunlight, bouncing around, just for you.
